summary:
I reviewed the whole slice diff (11f7ad9..HEAD). That covers LargestFiles.Top, making ScanStore's raw Size/OnDisk internal, the panel in MainWindow.xaml(.cs), the new WindowReport keys, the analysis rule and its twin and plants, LargestFilesTests, and cases L-001 to L-006 with the rescan hook. The code does what the design and its accepted dispositions say. Every departure from the design was declared in build attempt 1 or 2.

What I ran:
- `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`: 166 of 166 pass.
- LargestFilesScaleTests at 4,417,469 entries: Top(100) took 26.1 ms in Release (185.5 ms in Debug) and allocated 26,400 bytes.
- `rules-parity`: AGREE, 8 Facts, 11 twinned entries.
- Rules harness plants F17 to F19: each fires in both engines, as recorded.
- Fitness check: all 26 rules hold.
- WindowCases L-001 to L-006 on the republished exe: all pass. L-006's missing-root and begun shapes both fire. The hook log shows the list collapsed with 0 rows at the moment the second scan started.

Scanner.cs confirms that the store is frozen before ShowOutcome reads it. The scan runs on the caller's thread and returns only after Finish, with the canceller disposed first (Scanner.cs:12, 30-38, 275-297).

Every test on the case matrix feeds its shape in, and most assert the shape itself: the HardlinkDuplicate flag, the Link kind, sparse on-disk ≤ 4 KiB, path length > 260, and U+D800 at its position.

One minor issue, which I measured. The layout comment says an expanded unreadable-folders list "leaves room for" the largest-files list. At the default window size it does not: expanding a 12-folder unreadable list shrank LargestFilesPanel from 226 px to 26 px and pushed LargestFilesList out of view. L-003 only covers the collapsed expander.

findings.claim: When the person expands the unreadable-folders list at the default 880x600 window, the largest-files list is pushed out of view. The build moved UnreadableExpander to DockPanel.Dock=Bottom and capped UnreadableList at MaxHeight 200. The XAML comment then claims 'Its own list is capped, so opened it leaves room for theirs'. That is false: the expander is measured first and takes up to about 223 px, and LargestFilesPanel, the fill child, gets the remainder, which is less than its own header, caption, headings and 60 px minimum list. Measured on the published exe against a %TEMP% tree of 20 files and 12 list-denied folders, read through eng/read-window.ps1. Collapsed: LargestFilesPanel 226.46 px, LargestFilesList 170.58 px, inView True. Expanded (IsExpanded=true set by a throwaway startup hook, since deleted): UnreadableExpander 223 px, LargestFilesPanel 26.46 px, LargestFilesList inView False. A real C:\ scan leaves even less room: 663 unreadable folders in the spike, and a taller outcome section (the volume-coverage line wraps, and the probe-failure note shows). So on the slice's main use case, opening 'N folders could not be read' hides the whole list until the person collapses it again or enlarges the window. L-003 ('fit the list into the outcome panel … with the unreadable-folders list also filled') only reaches the collapsed state, because ShowOutcome sets IsExpanded=false. Nothing exercises the expanded state that the comment makes a claim about.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:40-45 (comment, DockPanel.Dock="Bottom", UnreadableList MaxHeight="200") and :50/:63 (LargestFilesPanel fill child, LargestFilesList MinHeight="60"); MainWindow.xaml.cs:311 (IsExpanded=false); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-L003 asserts inView only with the expander collapsed.
findings.fix: Make the two lists share the outcome space instead of letting the bottom-docked expander take all of it. For example, a Grid with the largest-files row at * and a MinHeight large enough for its header plus a few rows, and the expander row at Auto with UnreadableList's MaxHeight bound to a fraction of the available height. Then add an expanded variant to L-003 (a hook mode that sets UnreadableExpander.IsExpanded, which is a person's action and not the outcome under test) that asserts LargestFilesList.inView and UnreadableExpander.inView at the default size with at least 12 unreadable folders. Also correct the XAML comment.

obligations.evidence: Owed to validate, but it already holds by construction in the code. Scanner.cs:12 says the scan is 'Depth-first … on the caller's thread'. Scan (Scanner.cs:30-38) runs Run.Execute synchronously, and every store write is inside Run. Finish (275-287) only builds the ScanResult, and Run.Dispose (297) only disposes the reader. The SynchronousIoCancel canceller never writes the store and is disposed before Scan returns. ShowOutcome runs only after the awaited Task that returned the result (MainWindow.xaml.cs:159-193). So the ranking key cannot change during Top's pass for either Completed or Cancelled.

Same code as O-001. The scan has no background writers. LargestFiles.cs:21-22 records the contract ('Call it on the store of a returned ScanResult … Completed or Cancelled'), and MainWindow.ShowLargestFiles is reached only from ShowOutcome after Scan has returned.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LargestFilesTests.cs:20-43. deep.bin sits six folders down (a\b\c\d\e\f) and top.bin is at the root. Folder 'many' holds 5 x 1 MiB, more than any single file. The test asserts deep first and that 'many' is absent. The Kind==File filter is also proven by LargestFilesScaleTests, whose Terabyte-sized folder entries would outrank the planted files without it. Passed in my run.

LargestFilesTests.cs:46-71: 95 distinct sizes plus 10 files tied at 50x4 KiB, 105 in all, with count 100. It asserts 100 rows, no duplicate paths, that the 5 tied files kept are the 5 lowest indices, and that the result equals the prefix of a full sort. Passed.

LargestFilesTests.cs:74-94 covers an empty-folder root and a folder of 5 zero-length files plus a nested folder, as well as count 0, -1 and a null store. WindowCases Test-L004 checks the caption 'No non-empty files found.', 0 rows, a null first row and a hidden list. I ran it and it passed.
LargestFilesTests.cs:97-114 has a 3 MiB file in 1-first and its hardlink in 2-second. It asserts EntryFlags.HardlinkDuplicate on the second name and a list of exactly [first, one.bin].
LargestFilesTests.cs:117-138 creates a file symlink, a folder symlink and a junction through TempTree, asserts EntryKind.Link for all three, and expects the single row to be target.bin.

LargestFilesTests.cs:141-159 puts a 64 MiB sparse file (on-disk asserted ≤ 4 KiB) beside a 1 MiB dense file. The order is dense then sparse, with both sizes asserted, and Top(store, 1) keeps the dense file.

LargestFilesTests.cs:162-189 covers a path over 260 characters (asserted), 'ends-in-a-dot.', 'ends-in-a-space ' and 'a\uD800b.bin'. Each path must match exactly, contain no U+FFFD, and pass File.Exists on its \\?\ form.

LargestFilesTests.cs:192-216 cancels after 3 folders and gets Cancelled with the list [f1, f0]. WindowCases Test-L005, run by me, got Cancelled with 3 rows and the caption 'Top 3 of 90 files scanned in the part read before the scan stopped.'

WindowCases Test-L006 (WindowCases.ps1:1332-1401) and the rescan mode in StartupHook.cs:269-408. I ran it and both shapes passed. In the begun shape the hook logged 'listed rows=100 built=10 … largest=True' and then 'started scanning=True outcome=False largest=False rows=0', with the report showing LargestFilesPanel.visible false, largestFilesShown 0 and core null. The missing-root shape passed too. MainWindow.xaml.cs:139 and :380 are the two hides.

LargestFilesTests.cs:219-232 puts a 4 MiB file in a denied folder, and only readable.bin is listed. Test-L002, which I ran, checks the caption 'Top 2 of 2 files scanned. Files in 1 unreadable folder are not included.' and largestFileOnDisk 131072.

Test-L003, which I ran, has 105 files with the U+D800 name as the largest (row 0), plus a denied folder. It exited 0, with 7 of 100 rows realized and UnreadableExpander inView. It covers the collapsed expander only; see m1 for the expanded state.

Test-L001, which I ran, has files at three depths plus one empty file. It checks largestFilesShown 3, largestFileOnDisk 327680 and largestFilesMs 3.1. The panel is visible and laid out, and no 'plantedname' appears in the report. A missing root gives 0, null, null and a hidden panel.

LargestFilesTests.cs:269-335 builds a 4,417,469-entry store with the planted top 100 set exactly. I re-ran it: 26.1 ms in Release (185.5 ms in Debug), allocating 26,400 bytes. Checking the real C:\\ largestFilesMs against the 100 ms threshold stays with validate (m5).

ScanStore.cs:73 and :76 are now `internal long Size` and `internal long OnDisk`, and the remark is updated (ScanStore.cs:15-20). Grepping src finds the only raw readers at Scanner.cs:267-268. The App compiles without them.

WindowReport.cs adds LargestFilesPanel{visible,actualHeight} and LargestFilesList{inView,realizedRows}, and CheckLargestFiles asserts both in L-001 to L-005. ShowProblem calls HideLargestFiles (MainWindow.xaml.cs:380). L-006 now machine-checks the second-scan clearing.

MainWindow.xaml:63-81 sets ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Disabled" on LargestFilesList and HorizontalContentAlignment Stretch in ItemContainerStyle, and the path TextBlock has TextWrapping="Wrap".

Test-L003 plants 'a'+U+D800+'b-plantedname.bin' at 16x64 KiB as row 0. The report is written after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded) (WindowReport.cs), and an unhandled UI-thread exception would give exit 70 (App.xaml.cs). My run exited 0 with a report.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:334-339 produces 'Top {n} of {files} files scanned[ in the part read before the scan stopped].' and 'No non-empty files found[…].', with the unreadable suffix. L-002, L-003 and L-004 assert these exact strings.

The report carries largestFilesMs from the stopwatch around the single Top call (MainWindow.xaml.cs:330-332). The 100 ms threshold is recorded for validate. The Release measurement at 4.4M synthetic entries is 20-26 ms.

.taad/fitness.yaml:170-176 has the entry 'TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore (*.cs)' with (?m) and including_comments: true, above the first '# settled by' marker at line 185. It is twinned by ArchitectureRulesTests.TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore. In plants.json, F17 is `_store.Size(charged)` from Scanner.cs:267, F18 is `File.Delete(report)` and F19 is a comment. The harness runs I did were AS-RECORDED for all three, and rules-parity reports AGREE.
MainWindow.xaml.cs:319-322: ShowLargestFiles(result) is called after the UnreadableExpander block and before OutcomePanel is made visible and EndingShown is raised.

cases.evidence: LargestFilesTests.RanksFilesAtAnyDepthAndNeverAFolder puts deep.bin six folders down, top.bin at the root, and a 'many' folder of 5 x 1 MiB, more than any single file. It asserts deep first and no folder row. Real folders charge 0, so this test alone would not catch a missing Kind check, but LargestFilesScaleTests' Terabyte-sized folder entries would.

KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut: 95 distinct files plus 10 tied at the cut (105 files), with count 100. This runs the EnqueueDequeue path. It asserts the kept tied files by index and equality with a full-sort prefix.
ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList covers an empty-folder root and zero-length files. WindowCases L-004 (run) checks the 'No non-empty files found.' caption with no rows.
AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce: 3 MiB file plus a hardlink in another folder. It asserts HardlinkDuplicate on the second name, so the shape really is fed in.
NoRowComesFromALink creates a file symlink, a folder symlink and a junction, each asserted as EntryKind.Link, and expects one row, the target.

RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes: a 64 MiB sparse file with on-disk asserted ≤ 4 KiB, beside a dense 1 MiB file. Dense ranks first, the sparse file is still listed with both sizes, and Top(1) keeps the dense one.
EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath: a path over 260 characters (asserted), trailing dot, trailing space, and U+D800 (asserted at its position). Paths must match exactly and exist via \\?\.
AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead asserts ScanStatus.Cancelled and the partial list [f1, f0]. L-005 (run): a Stop through the hook, Cancelled, 3 rows and the partial-scan caption.

L-006 (run, passed). Both shapes are fed in: a second scan whose root has been moved aside (RootUnreadable) and a second scan that has begun. The hook log proves the first list was bound and laid out, then collapsed with 0 rows once the second scan started.

AFileInAFolderTheScanCouldNotReadIsNotListed puts the 4 MiB file in a list-denied folder. L-002 (run) puts the 2 MiB file in a denied folder and asserts the caption 'Files in 1 unreadable folder are not included.'

L-003 (run): 100 of 105 rows, row 0 a U+D800 name, and a denied folder so the unreadable list is filled. It exits 0 with 7 rows realized and both controls inView. The expander is only ever collapsed (ShowOutcome sets IsExpanded=false). The expanded state is not exercised, and I measured that it pushes the list out (m1).
L-001 (run): a finished scan of a planted tree at three depths. The scalars are checked against the tree, the panel is visible and in view, and no planted name is in the report.

LargestFilesScaleTests builds a real ScanStore of 4,417,469 entries with larger decoy links, hardlink duplicates and folders. Re-run: 26.1 ms in Release, 26,400 bytes allocated. Reading the real C:\\ largestFilesMs against 100 ms is validate's (m5).

The design marks this case material:false, and no test feeds a probed, probe-failed or online-only file into Top. The deferral still holds against the code: LargestFiles.cs reads only Kind, ChargedSize, ChargedOnDisk and GetPath and never branches on Flags, and the sparse case in C-006 models the logical>0 with on-disk≈0 shape.

drift: Nothing departs from the design undeclared. I checked the declared departures against the tree and they are all there as described. (1) Layout: LargestFilesPanel is the DockPanel fill child, not a ListBox with a fixed MaxHeight. UnreadableExpander is docked at the bottom, and UnreadableList gained MaxHeight=200. That last cap also changes the earlier slice's expanded unreadable list, which used to fill the panel. (2) The report gained more window keys than the design named: LargestFilesCaption, LargestFilesList{actualHeight,inView,realizedRows} and UnreadableExpander{visible,actualHeight,inView}. (3) The rule became the twinned entry 'TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore (*.cs)', and RuleCases.ps1's settled counts, which were wrong at HEAD, were corrected. (4) The C-009 second-scan check became window case L-006, driven by raising Loaded from the hook, where the design put it on the validate drive list.

The design text still says index order is 'multithreaded' and that a Cancelled-scan test 'settles' the writer invariant. The code and the M1/m3 dispositions correct both (LargestFiles.cs:12-14, 21-22). Anyone reading the design document alone should know it is wrong on these two points.
